problems: stop 1 card 4, answer 2: copies a Prep line word for word

explanations.explanation: You got it, baker! David says, "I shall not want" (Psalm 23:1). That old phrase means he will not lack a single thing he needs. When the Almighty is the one holding the staff, you are taken care of from top to bottom.
Not earn, friend. David says, "I shall not want" (Psalm 23:1). A sheep doesn't clock in for a shift to buy its own grass. The shepherd provides everything, so David won't lack a thing.
Not lose, baker. David says, "I shall not want" (Psalm 23:1). That means he will not lack anything he needs. The good Shepherd keeps His flock supplied so nobody goes hungry.
Spot on, baker! Lush green grass and calm, still water mean a sheep can stop pacing and finally sit down. The LORD gives David real rest for his weary bones (Psalm 23:2). That is true peace.

No hustle here, friend. David says the LORD makes him lie down in green pastures and leads him beside quiet waters (Psalm 23:2). Sheep do not lie down when they are clocking overtime. This is a scene of deep rest and quiet peace.
Not danger, baker. Green pastures and quiet waters mean the sheep is totally safe and fed (Psalm 23:2). A nervous sheep will not even lie down if there is trouble around. This is pure rest.
You nailed it, baker! David writes, "He restores my soul" (Psalm 23:3). Life can drain you flat out, but the LORD brings fresh life right back into David's heart. That is deep renewal.
Not tests, friend. David says, "He restores my soul" (Psalm 23:3). The LORD isn't handing out a pop quiz here. He is reviving David from the inside out.
Not weighs, baker. David writes, "He restores my soul" (Psalm 23:3). The LORD isn't setting David on a scale to inspect him. He is refreshing David's spirit and giving him new strength.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His name
explanations.explanation: That's the truth, baker! David says the LORD guides him in right paths "for the sake of His name" (Psalm 23:3). God's own good name is on the line when He leads His people. He stays faithful because that is who He is.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His flock
explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. The flock gets blessed, but David says the LORD leads him "for the sake of His name" (Psalm 23:3). God's own name and honor stand behind how faithfully He guides.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His land
explanations.explanation: Not the land, baker. David says the LORD leads him "for the sake of His name" (Psalm 23:3). God's own reputation is tied to how He leads His servant. He does it to show His faithful name.

explanations.answer: Because the LORD is with him
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker! David says, "I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Psalm 23:4). The valley is dark and scary, but David isn't walking it alone. Having the Shepherd right beside him clears out the fear.

Not on his own strength, friend. A sheep trying to flex in a dark canyon is in big trouble. David says, "I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Psalm 23:4). His peace comes from the Shepherd's presence.
Not because it's a short trip, baker. Valleys can drag on for a long time. David doesn't fear because the LORD is right there walking beside him (Psalm 23:4). That presence makes all the difference.

True it is, baker! David says, "Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me" (Psalm 23:4). That rod drives off the wolves, and that staff pulls a stray sheep out of the ditch. In the Shepherd's hands, those tools bring deep comfort.

It's actually true, friend! David sings, "Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me" (Psalm 23:4). In the hands of a good shepherd, those heavy sticks mean protection from predators and rescue from the briars. That gives David real peace.

You got it, baker! David says, "You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies" (Psalm 23:5). God invites him to sit down like an honored guest and enjoy a feast. That is top-tier hospitality.
Not a tent, friend. David says the LORD prepares a "table" before him (Psalm 23:5). The picture switches to a grand host laying out a full banquet for His guest. It is time to eat, not pitch camp.
Not a bed, baker. David says, "You prepare a table before me" (Psalm 23:5). God isn't setting him up for a nap here. He is rolling out a royal meal with overflowing hospitality.

Actually, it's false, friend! David says the LORD prepares a table "in the presence of my enemies" (Psalm 23:5). God doesn't even bother to sneak David out of the neighborhood. The foes have to stand right there and watch God bless him.

You're right, it's false, baker! David says God prepares his table "in the presence of my enemies" (Psalm 23:5). God sets out the feast right in front of them. The enemies just have to stand there and watch David dine in peace.

Spot on, baker! When David says, "my cup overflows" (Psalm 23:5), he means God's blessings don't stop at the rim. God doesn't measure out His goodness with an eye dropper. He pours until it spills over the sides.

Nobody spilled the juice, friend! An overflowing cup is a picture of total abundance (Psalm 23:5). The host keeps pouring the finest drink because He delights in blessing His guest with more than enough.
Not rushed at all, baker. An overflowing cup doesn't mean someone bumped the table in a hurry. David is saying God fills his life so high with goodness that it spills over the edges (Psalm 23:5).
You got it, baker! David says, "Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life" (Psalm 23:6). Those two don't just trail along at a distance. They pursue him everywhere he goes.

Not wealth and honor, friend. David looks down the road and sees "goodness and mercy" chasing after him (Psalm 23:6). Gold can vanish overnight, but God's steady mercy sticks around for the whole trip.
Not strength and wisdom, baker. David says, "Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life" (Psalm 23:6). God's loyal love and kindness stay right on his heels every single day.

explanations.answer: In the house of the LORD
explanations.explanation: Right on the money, baker! David wraps up his song by saying, "and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever" (Psalm 23:6). He isn't just dropping in for a weekend visit. He has an eternal home right with his God.
Not Hebron, friend. David spent time in cities, but his song ends with his eyes on God's home: "and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever" (Psalm 23:6). That is where he plans to stay.

Not just a piece of earthly land, baker. David closes his song looking way higher: "and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever" (Psalm 23:6). Living right in the presence of God is the real finish line.
